targetTest: start records the brief file as a task reference: provider manual-brief, kind brief-file, the real path, the digest of its bytes, fresh
expected: after start the run has one task_refs row (manual-brief, brief-file, the brief realpath, sha256 of its bytes, fresh); after the brief is edited, resume moves the run to blocked_on_decision with reason ref_changed, opens one decision naming the brief and launches no unit; a deleted brief gives ref_deleted
actual: task_refs has no writer: the row count is 0 (expected 1); resume of an edited or deleted brief exits 0 and the run goes on (a non-zero exit and a blocked run were planned); the later cases read rows that do not exist; 5 of 5 cases fail
failingTests: start records the brief file as a task reference: provider manual-brief, kind brief-file, the real path, the digest of its bytes, fresh
after the brief is edited, resume blocks the run: blocked_on_decision with reason ref_changed, one open decision naming the brief, no unit launched
the reference is now `changed` and still names the digest the run was built from
resume moves the run to blocked_on_decision with reason ref_deleted and marks the reference deleted
the reference is refreshed to fresh and the run goes on to ready_for_review
summary: RED: 5 of undefined fail on assertions against skeleton exports that carry the planned names and no behavior
semanticAssessment: The target ran to its assertion: the real CLI started a run, the supervisor was killed by SIGKILL at after-checkpoint:context-pack#2 and the run was resumed. The target failed on the planned assertion assert.equal(refs.length, 1) (actual 0) because nothing writes task_refs, and the resume cases fail on assert.notEqual(resumed.code, 0) because nothing refreshes a reference. No import, syntax, fixture or zero-test fault: the same fixtures drive the passing run-resume suite.
